title: Choose SettleUp's visual world
question: Your sketchbook brief leads. Lock it, choose a close alternate, or re-roll the open structural details.

options.label: The Shared Ledger Study
options.lineage: industrial-design sketchbooks crossed with annotated bank ledgers
options.thesis: A real bank charge becomes a shared agreement on the same sheet where the friend group gathers.
options.viewport: A portrait phone fills the opening frame with one real transaction under review; scrolling pulls the camera back until it becomes one of six phones arranged in a connected circle.
options.risk: The drawn language must never make amounts, status, or actions feel approximate.

raised.raise: The scroll sequence has discrete, legible transaction beats instead of decorative drift.
Every connector and rotation reads as a physical joint with tension and purpose.
The signed-in screens preserve compact information hierarchy beneath the expressive landing story.

options.label: The Field Note Constellation
options.lineage: naturalist field journals and hand-plotted social maps
options.thesis: Transactions are observed specimens; the friend group is the map that gives each one meaning.
options.viewport: A bank charge is pinned like a field specimen beside a hand-plotted group map; the scroll traces its path from account to friends to settled balance.
options.risk: Its familiar notebook metaphor is clear but less singular than the phone-circle ritual.

options.label: The Paper Phone Circle
options.lineage: hand-cranked paper automata and pinned mechanical toys
options.thesis: Each phone is a jointed paper figure; one scroll-crank assembles the group and passes a transaction around it.
options.viewport: A cut-paper phone stands alone above a small crank line; scrolling turns the crank and unfolds a ring of connected phones around the shared charge.
options.case: It identifies strongly with the group ritual and makes the motion physical, but the cut-paper vocabulary communicates bank data less directly than the ledger study.
options.risk: Too much dimensional craft could make a trustworthy finance workflow feel toy-like.

options.label: Transaction Cutting Bench
options.lineage: film editing workprints and pinned trims
options.thesis: Imported charges move through a perforated review strip and completed splits receive grease-pencil marks.
options.viewport: A horizontal transaction strip scrubs beneath a fixed review frame.
options.case: The sequential review is useful, but the editing ritual does not identify with friend groups.
options.kept: Discrete scroll beats and a visible place marker keep the story understandable.
options.risk: The film metaphor competes with the bank-to-group mechanism.

options.label: Dense Utility Mosaic
options.thesis: Accounts, charges, groups, and balances tile into a rigorous mobile information mosaic.
options.viewport: The first phone shows a dense live bank feed with one transaction already routed to friends.
options.case: It protects product clarity but loses the spacious, idea-driven group ritual requested for the landing page.
options.kept: Compact hierarchy governs the signed-in application rather than the expressive landing sequence.
options.risk: Density can feel administrative during a casual social task.

options.label: Glyph Circle
options.lineage: live ASCII scenes and character-grid rendering
options.thesis: The phone circle resolves from transaction symbols as the visitor changes viewing distance.
options.viewport: A close-up amount becomes a complete social diagram when the glyph field zooms out.
options.case: Distance-based revelation is strong, but a strict character grid conflicts with the human hand-drawn brief.
options.kept: The composition must read differently—and meaningfully—at close, middle, and distant scales.
options.risk: It codes the product as technical rather than social.

canonCard.label: The polished finance-app standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean bank feed, friendly avatars, balance cards, and a familiar product screenshot hero.
canonCard.viewport: A concise headline and CTA sit beside a polished phone showing imported transactions and group balances.
canonCard.risk: Immediately understandable, but visually interchangeable with other finance products.
